title: The London everyone knows
subtopic: T6a — the landmarks, and which of them Fogg could and could not have seen
learning_goal: Place the famous London landmarks in time against 1872: Big Ben new, Parliament rebuilt, Fogg's London Bridge now in Arizona, Tower Bridge not yet built.

narration.script: It starts in London — so first, the London a visitor comes for. The clock tower at Westminster, and the bell inside it that everyone calls Big Ben. Strictly, Big Ben is only the bell. When Fogg left, the tower was thirteen years old. The Houses of Parliament around it had been rebuilt after a fire in eighteen thirty-four. London Bridge — Fogg's London Bridge — was a stone bridge opened in eighteen thirty-one. In nineteen sixty-eight it was sold to an American businessman for about a million pounds, taken apart, shipped across the Atlantic and rebuilt in the Arizona desert. It still stands there, in Lake Havasu City. And Tower Bridge — the one on every postcard — Fogg never saw at all. It opened in eighteen ninety-four, twenty-two years after he left. So the city he set out from was brand new in some places, and not yet built in others.

review.notes:
ADDED 2026-09-11 on founder feedback: "for a total outsider, seems natural to flash some more famous landmark like big ben westminster london bridge etc before diving into savile row or reform club. remember this is a travel+book show."
New facts researched 2026-09-11 (F-N15..F-N18, not yet on a fact sheet): Big Ben is strictly the bell; tower completed 31 May 1859, bell first chimed 11 July 1859; Palace of Westminster largely destroyed by fire 16 Oct 1834; Rennie's London Bridge opened 1 Aug 1831, sold April 1968 to Robert P. McCulloch for £1.02 m, rededicated at Lake Havasu City 10 Oct 1971; Tower Bridge opened 30 June 1894.
The 'buyer thought it was Tower Bridge' story is DENIED by both parties and must not be used.
